title: JRE 2230 - Evan Hafer
guestBio: Evan Hafer is a Special Forces veteran, founder/CEO of Black Rifle Coffee Company, and one of the hosts of the "Black Rifle Coffee Podcast."
tldr: Evan Hafer discusses his journey from Special Forces to founding Black Rifle Coffee Company
The conversation covers military experience and what shaped his perspective on business and leadership
Black Rifle Coffee's growth strategy and how the brand resonates with a specific audience
Discussion about veteran entrepreneurship and supporting the military community
Hafer shares insights on building company culture and connecting with customers authentically
The podcast covers current events and how they impact the coffee business and veteran community
recap:
Joe Rogan sits down with Evan Hafer in episode 2230, diving deep into the world of Black Rifle Coffee Company and what it takes to build a brand from the ground up as a Special Forces veteran. Hafer brings a unique perspective shaped by years of military service, and he doesn't shy away from discussing how that experience fundamentally changed his approach to business and life.

The episode explores Hafer's transition from active duty to entrepreneurship, which wasn't a straightforward path. He talks about identifying a gap in the market and how Black Rifle Coffee filled that void by creating a brand that actually represented the values of the military and veteran community, rather than just slapping a flag on a product. Joe and Evan get into the nitty gritty of building a company culture that matters, one where employees understand they're part of something bigger than just selling coffee.

Hafer is candid about the challenges of scaling a business while maintaining authenticity. He discusses how Black Rifle Coffee became more than just a product - it became a movement and a lifestyle brand that connected with people who felt alienated by mainstream corporate messaging. The conversation touches on how social media and direct customer engagement allowed them to build a community rather than just a customer base.

Throughout the episode, Hafer emphasizes the importance of hiring the right people and creating an environment where veterans and like-minded individuals can thrive. He shares stories from his military background that inform his leadership philosophy, and Joe picks up on the themes of discipline, loyalty, and purpose that run through both military service and successful entrepreneurship.

The discussion also covers the Black Rifle Coffee Podcast and how that platform extends the brand's reach beyond just coffee. Hafer talks about having genuine conversations and not being afraid to tackle controversial topics or disagree with mainstream narratives. Joe and Evan bond over the idea of building authentic platforms in an increasingly corporatized media landscape.

quotes: You build a company with people who share your values, not just people who need a job.
The military taught me that mission comes first, and everything else follows from that.
We didn't want to just sell coffee to veterans, we wanted to build a community.
